questions.question: Based on our pace and what's left, should we ask the client for more doors, or a second pass on the turf we have?

args.query: should we ask the client for more doors or a second pass on the turf we have

args.sql:
SELECT
  (SELECT round(avg_daily_doors_last_7d,1) FROM v_office_pace WHERE office='All offices') AS avg_daily_doors_last_7d,
  (SELECT knocking_days_left FROM v_office_pace WHERE office='All offices') AS knocking_days_left,
  (SELECT round(avg_daily_doors_last_7d * knocking_days_left,0) FROM v_office_pace WHERE office='All offices') AS projected_capacity_remaining,
  (SELECT sum(doors_untouched) FROM v_precinct_coverage) AS untouched_doors_left,
  (SELECT sum(not_home_doors) FROM v_precinct_coverage) AS not_home_doors

sources.text: When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

questions.answer:
Based on the program's own rule, we should ask the client for more doors first.

- Projected capacity for the rest of the program: 1489.1 doors/day × 16 days left = 23,826 doors [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched (first-pass) doors still in our turf: 10,393 [table:v_precinct_coverage]
- Because capacity (23,826) is larger than the untouched doors left (10,393), we will run out of first-pass turf before the program ends [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
- The rule says to ask the client for more doors first, since new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
- A second pass on not-home doors (18,555 of them) is only the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]

How it's worked out: projected capacity = average daily doors of the last 7 days × days left; if that exceeds the untouched doors left in the turf, we run out of first-pass turf and should ask for more doors before falling back to a second pass [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass].

questions.question: Why does the client's daily report show more doors than our dashboard for Oct 12?

args.query: client daily report doors counted attempts vs dashboard doors

args.sql: SELECT office, doors, contacts, attempts, rolled_back_attempts FROM v_daily_doors WHERE knock_date = '2026-10-12'
SELECT office, doors_reported, contacts_reported FROM client_daily_report WHERE report_date = '2026-10-12'

sources.text: The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

An attempt is every knock record the canvassing app submits. If a canvasser knocks a not-home door at 11:00 and comes back at 14:00, that is two attempts and one door. Attempts are always equal to or higher than doors.

The client receives a daily report per office pulled from the canvassing app at the end of each day. It lists attempts (labeled "doors" in the client's sheet) and contacts as submitted, before any QC rollback. We do not edit a daily report after it is sent.

questions.answer:
The client's sheet counts every attempt (each knock record) and is pulled before any QC rollback, while our dashboard counts each door once per day with rolled-back attempts removed — so the client's number is always equal to or higher than ours.

- Eastgate: client shows 498 "doors" vs 342 on the dashboard; the gap is 142 rolled-back attempts plus repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors] [table:client_daily_report]
- Harbor: client shows 428 vs 406 doors; no rollbacks, so the 22-door gap is repeat attempts at the same door [table:v_daily_doors] [table:client_daily_report]
- Northside: client shows 558 vs 533 doors; no rollbacks, so the 25-door gap is repeat attempts [table:v_daily_doors] [table:client_daily_report]
- A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts; a larger gap (like Eastgate's) almost always means a rollback [doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]

How it's worked out: the client's "doors" column is actually attempts pulled at end of day before QC rollback, while the dashboard counts each door once per day with rollbacks removed, so the difference is repeat attempts plus any rolled-back attempts [doc:client-reporting#daily-report] [doc:counting-doors#attempts].

questions.question: Which offices or canvassers have the most duplicate registrations, and is it one person or across the board?
questions.answer:
It's one person: Renata Cole at Harbor accounts for 42 of the program's 112 duplicate registrations (37.5%), while everyone else is at single digits.

- Harbor as an office has 66 of 112 program duplicates (59%), but that's almost entirely Renata Cole's 42 [table:v_vr_pace]
- Northside has 24 duplicates spread across its canvassers (max 7), Eastgate 22 (max 6) [table:v_vr_pace]
- Program-wide: 112 duplicates out of 3,781 cards collected, a 3.0% rate [table:v_vr_pace]

args.query: QC calls, confirmation, unreachable, wrong information

sources.text: A sample of valid cards gets a QC call a day or two after collection. Outcomes are confirmed (the registrant confirms they filled out the card), unreachable (no answer after two tries) and wrong_info (the person says the details are wrong or they did not register). Wrong information above 10 percent of calls for a canvasser is escalated.

When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.
